definitions.explanation: Moving or acting slowly and inefficiently, often causing frustration. Implies wasting time or being indecisive.

examples.japanese: もたもたしてる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{遅刻|ちこく}する→遅刻する：22282_chikokusuru⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you keep dilly-dallying, you'll be late.

examples.japanese: もたもた⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{早|はや}く→早い：00514_hayai⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}して→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧。
examples.english: Stop dawdling and get ready quickly.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧もたもた⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{動|うご}き→動き：11926_ugoki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧イライラ⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I got irritated by his sluggish movements.

notes:
MIMETIC TYPE:
Onomatopoeia expressing slow, inefficient movement or action.

GRAMMATICAL FORMS:
- もたもた⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ - to dawdle, be slow (suru-verb)
- もたもた（⟦と→と：00512_to⟧）⟦{動|うご}く→動く：00904_ugoku⟧ - to move sluggishly
- もたもた⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧ - sluggish (adjectival)

USAGE:
Usually carries a negative connotation, implying the person is being annoyingly slow or wasting time. Often used when urging someone to hurry.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ぐずぐずする→ぐずぐずする：25850_guzuguzusuru⟧ - to dawdle, procrastinate
- ⟦のろのろ→のろのろ：05162_noronoro⟧ - slowly (more neutral)
- ⟦てきぱき→てきぱき：05649_tekipaki⟧ - briskly, efficiently (opposite)
